definition: One of the Group 1 metals (lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium) — soft, low-density metals that react with water to give strongly alkaline hydroxide solutions.
msAccepts: a Group 1 metal that reacts with water forming an alkaline hydroxide solution and hydrogen
soft reactive metal stored under oil
msAvoids: any metal in Group 2 or the transition block
metals that simply do not react with water

definition: The arrangement of an atom's electrons among its shells, written as numbers per shell — e.g. sodium 2,8,1. The outermost number controls the atom's chemistry.
msAccepts: the number of electrons in each shell (e.g. 2,8,1)
how electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus
msAvoids: just the total number of electrons
a diagram of protons and neutrons

definition: A negative ion, OH⁻, carrying a 1− charge. Alkali metals form hydroxides with the formula MOH, whose aqueous solutions are strongly alkaline.
msAccepts: OH⁻ ion; metal compounds with formula MOH giving alkaline solutions
the ion made of one oxygen and one hydrogen with a 1− charge
msAvoids: calling it a negative metal ion
confusing it with water H₂O or oxide O²⁻

definition: A compound of a metal with oxygen. Alkali metals react with oxygen in the air to form oxide coatings such as M₂O.
msAccepts: a compound of the metal with oxygen (e.g. Na₂O)
the coating formed when an alkali metal reacts with air
msAvoids: the oxide as a positive ion
confusing with hydroxide (which contains hydrogen as well)

definition: A Group 7 non-metal (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine), written X in family equations. Alkali metals react with halogens to form salts with the formula MX.
msAccepts: a Group 7 element; reacts with an alkali metal to give an ionic salt MX
msAvoids: placing halogens in Group 1
saying halogens are metals

definition: A charged particle formed when an atom gains or loses electrons. Group 1 atoms lose their single outer electron to form 1+ ions (M⁺), which are colourless.
msAccepts: an atom that has lost or gained electrons so it carries a charge
Group 1 metals form 1+ ions by losing the outer electron
msAvoids: an atom changing its proton count
ions formed by sharing electrons

definition: Having a pH greater than 7 — the property of a solution of a soluble base (an alkali). Alkali metal hydroxide solutions are strongly alkaline.
msAccepts: pH above 7; turns universal indicator blue/purple
the solution contains hydroxide ions and is a strong base
msAvoids: describing the metal itself as alkaline
confusing alkaline with acidic (pH below 7)

definition: To lose shininess because the fresh metal surface reacts with oxygen in the air, growing a dull oxide coating. Tarnishing speed ranks the Group 1 reactivity trend.
msAccepts: the shiny surface goes dull as it reacts with oxygen forming an oxide layer
freshly cut metal dulls in seconds/minutes in air
msAvoids: calling it rusting (that is iron-specific)
saying the metal melts or dissolves in air

definition: Melted by heat into a liquid state. Sodium in its water reaction is momentarily molten — the reaction's own heat melts it into a ball — though the equation keeps (s).
msAccepts: the metal has melted to a liquid because of the heat released
sodium ball on water is molten sodium
msAvoids: confusing molten with dissolved in water
writing state symbol (l) for sodium in this equation (examiners expect (s))

definition: Mass per unit volume (g/cm³). Lithium, sodium and potassium are less dense than water so float; densities rise only irregularly down Group 1.
msAccepts: mass per unit volume; Li/Na/K float on water because their density is below 1 g/cm³
msAvoids: confusing density with weight
claiming density rises smoothly down the group (it is irregular)

definition: Giving out radiation from an unstable nucleus that decays over time. Francium is extremely radioactive and short-lived, so it is never seen as a visible sample.
msAccepts: unstable nucleus that decays emitting radiation
francium decays so fast that only ~20–30 g exist in the crust at any time
msAvoids: saying radioactivity is a chemical reaction
confusing radioactive with reactive

definition: One of the forms of an element with the same proton number but different neutron numbers. Uranium-235 decay produces a francium isotope.
msAccepts: atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
same protons, different mass number
msAvoids: saying isotopes are different elements
defining isotopes by electron count
